newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bank of Korea governor says won level acceptable.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea governor says won level acceptable.

text.p: Bank of Korea Governor Kyung Shik Lee said on Thursday that the current level of the won was acceptable and the central bank's focus was on currency stability.
"I think the current level is acceptable so I want it (the won) to be stable," he told Reuters Financial Television.
Referring to the recent failure of Hanbo Steel Corp and its impact on the financial markets in Korea the Governor said, "The Hanbo problem is not a fundamental one."
"The effect on the economy (from Hanbo) is not so serious," he added. "It's just a scandal.
"Other measures are not necessary ... the Hanbo scandal does not need any extra money," he added.
Kyung's comments came as the won fell to an 84-month low of of 871.00 against the dollar in early morning trade.

Intervention by the Bank of Korea, which sold about $40 million when the dollar hit 887.00 in three-month and 899.00 in six-month forward trading, did not help and at the lunch break spot won was quoted a morning low of 875.10.
"The greenback will remain strong due to the dollar's rise in world markets," said a local bank dealer.
He forecast advance dollar buying in preparation of import deals next week would also pull the won down.
Dealers said the won's depreciation would continue unless economic fundamentals turned around or the dollar stumbled on global financial markets.
